app.title: AstroStretch
app.summary: A person loads a built-in sample image or uploads their own FITS file. The interface takes the first two-dimensional image in the file and shows its size, usable pixel count, median and dynamic range, plus header details in a section that opens and closes. The person picks a stretch method and strength and sets black and white points as percentiles. The original and stretched images appear side by side, above a pixel-value histogram that marks the current display limits. The stretched view can be downloaded as a PNG, and the original measurements stay unchanged.

task.text: Pick display limits and a nonlinear brightness stretch that bring out faint structure in a raw single-band image, then export the result for display.

data.text: A single two-dimensional grayscale image of raw instrument intensities, with header metadata.
data.item: one pixel of a two-dimensional telescope image

stage.text: exploring a raw telescope image for display, before calibration or measurement

mechanism.text: The method selector, strength slider and percentile sliders control a single rescale-and-stretch step. Each change redraws the stretched image next to the untouched original and moves the black and white point lines on a log-scaled pixel histogram.

field.text: image display stretching of FITS data in astronomy

workflow.name: tune a display transform on one image and export the rendered result

steps.here: radio choice between a synthetic sample nebula and a FITS upload (.fits/.fit/.fts); the first 2-D HDU is used

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: metrics for image size, usable pixels, median and dynamic range, plus an expander showing the OBJECT, FILTER, EXPTIME and DATE-OBS header values

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Linear, Logarithmic or Asinh stretch with a strength slider (off for Linear), after clipping to black and white points set as percentiles
original view next to the stretched view, redrawn each time a control changes

steps.step: check the settings against the value distribution
steps.here: log-count histogram of pixel values with red and blue lines at the current black and white points
'Download stretched PNG' saves the displayed stretch as <name>_stretched.png

distinctive: Black and white points are set as percentiles of the finite pixels instead of absolute values, so a few extreme or faulty pixels can't set the display range.
The stretches are nonlinear (log1p and arcsinh), each normalized by its strength so output stays between 0 and 1.
The histogram trims its tails to the 0.1–99.9 percentiles and subsamples large images so the plot stays readable and responsive.
The export is for display only: the original FITS measurements are never changed.
